q: A company sells goods on credit in November and the customer pays in January. Which statement is correct for the year-end?
choices: Revenue is recognized in January when cash is received
Revenue is recognized in November, even though no cash is received yet
No revenue is recognized until the invoice is paid
Revenue is recognized when the goods are ordered
explain: Under accrual accounting, revenue is recognized when goods are delivered or the service is rendered, not when the customer pays.

q: Under the three types of purchases, an electricity invoice is recorded as:
choices: An expense upon receipt of the invoice
Inventory, expensed when removed from stock
An expense only when it is paid in cash
explain: Services such as electricity are expenses, deemed consumed when the invoice is received.

q: A sale of merchandise on credit is recorded with two transactions. What are they?
choices: Purchase of inventory and trade payable
The sale (revenue and trade receivable) and the inventory drawdown (cost of sales)
explain: A sale of goods creates revenue with a receivable, plus a cost of sales that reduces inventories.

q: On 1 July the company borrows 10,000 from the bank. On 30 Dec it repays 3,000. What amount is still owed at 31 Dec?
explain: Balance = |debits - credits| = 10,000 - 3,000 = 7,000.

q: A company has taxable profit of 200,000 and a tax rate of 17%. What is the income tax expense?
explain: Income tax = taxable profit x rate = 200,000 x 17% = 34,000 (166,000 would be profit after tax).

q: Which cost is excluded from the acquisition cost of a machine and recorded as an expense?
choices: Staff training on how to use the machine
explain: Training, maintenance and administrative costs are expenses; transport, installation and tests make the asset ready for use.

q: Which fixed asset is NOT depreciated?
explain: Land and non-current financial assets are not depreciated; they have no limited useful life.

q: Under straight-line depreciation, what is the annual depreciation rate for an asset with a 5-year useful life?
explain: Rate = 100% / useful life = 100% / 5 = 20%.

q: A company has 5,000 shares with a par value of 8. What is its share capital?
explain: Share capital = number of shares x par value = 5,000 x 8 = 40,000.

q: Which equation correctly gives equity?
explain: From Assets = Equity + Liabilities, Equity = Assets - Liabilities.

q: On the balance sheet, prepaid expenses are presented as:
explain: A prepaid expense is an asset: the company has paid for goods or services it will receive after the closing date.

q: On the balance sheet, deferred revenue is presented as:
explain: The company has recorded income but still has to provide the service, so it is a liability.

q: A company has 25,000 in bank account A and an overdraft of 4,000 on account B. What is its net cash?
explain: Net cash = cash and cash equivalents - bank overdrafts = 25,000 - 4,000 = 21,000.

q: Which is a condition for recognizing a provision at the closing date?
choices: A present obligation arising from a past event
A management decision to renovate next year
Cash already set aside to pay
explain: A provision requires an obligation from a past event, a probable outflow and a reliable estimate; future intentions do not qualify.

q: Machine: price 50,000, 10% discount, transport 1,500, installation 2,500, staff training 2,000. What is the acquisition cost?
Cost 36,000, straight-line, 6-year life, available for use on 1 October X1. What is the X1 depreciation expense?
explain: 36,000 x (1/6) x 3/12 = 1,500 (pro rata temporis of 3 months).

q: Machine cost 24,000, 4-year life, straight-line, available 1 July X1. Carrying amount at 31/12/X2?
Merchandise bought for 1,000 on credit (not yet sold). What is the immediate effect?
choices: Inventories +1,000 and trade payables +1,000; no effect on profit
explain: Merchandise is an inventory asset; it becomes an expense (cost of sales) only when removed from inventory.

q: Goods costing 600 are sold on credit for 900. What is the effect on profit?
explain: Revenue 900 minus cost of sales 600 = +300.

q: Income 900,000 and expenses 600,000; tax rate 20%. What is net profit after tax?
Par value 10. The company issues 3,000 new shares at an issue price of 14. What is the share premium?
A 80,000 loan at 5% is repaid in equal principal of 16,000 per year, interest paid on the opening balance. Interest for year 2?
On 1 Nov the company borrows 120,000 at 6%, interest payable annually on 31 Oct. Accrued interest at 31 Dec?
On 1 Oct the company pays 12,000 for 12 months of insurance, fully expensed. Prepaid expense at 31 Dec?
explain: 9 months remain after 31 Dec: 12,000 x 9/12 = 9,000.

q: On 1 Nov a client pays 6,000 for 6 months of service, recorded as income. Deferred revenue at 31 Dec?
explain: 4 of 6 months remain unprovided: 6,000 x 4/6 = 4,000.

q: Inventory cost 5,000, net realizable value 4,200, accumulated impairment already 300. What is the impairment loss for the year?
explain: Required accumulated impairment = 5,000 - 4,200 = 800; loss = 800 - 300 = 500.

q: A trade receivable of 10,000 is expected to be only 60% collected. Required impairment?
explain: Expected collection 6,000; required impairment = 10,000 - 6,000 = 4,000.

q: Opening cash 20,000; operating cash flow -5,000; investing -12,000; financing +30,000. Closing cash?
Machine cost 24,000, 4-year life, straight-line, available 1 April X1. What is the carrying amount at 31/12/X3?
explain: X1: 24,000 x 25% x 9/12 = 4,500; X2 and X3: 6,000 each. Accumulated 16,500; carrying amount 7,500.

q: A 6,000 provision was set up for a lawsuit. The company is ordered to pay 7,500. Effect on the next year's profit?
choices: Decrease of 1,500 in cash only, no profit effect
explain: The provision of 6,000 is used; the extra 7,500 - 6,000 = 1,500 is a new expense.

q: Profit before adjustments 50,000. Unbilled electricity 500; prepaid expense 1,000 (already expensed); accrued interest 625; unbilled consulting revenue 2,000. Adjusted profit?
explain: 50,000 - 500 (expense) + 1,000 (expense removed) - 625 (interest) + 2,000 (revenue) = 51,875.

q: Capital 100,000 (10,000 shares, par 10). 2,000 shares issued at 15; year profit 8,000. Book value per share?
Profit before tax 400,000, tax rate 25%, tax paid next year. At year-end, net profit and tax liability?
explain: Tax expense 100,000 is a liability until paid; net profit = 400,000 - 100,000 = 300,000; no cash moves this year.

q: Asset carrying amount 18,000; fair value less costs of disposal 12,000; value in use 15,000. Impairment loss?
Year 1: a machine costing 24,000 is paid in cash on 1 Jan; 4-year life, straight-line. Effect on profit and cash in year 1 (nothing else)?
explain: Depreciation 24,000 x 25% = 6,000 hits profit; the full 24,000 paid is an investing cash outflow.
